title: Yielding Middle Eastern Rice Fatteh
description: A mustardy, velvety rice dish shaped like nigiri, served in a cazuela for a romantic date night.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear.
Heat the olive oil in a cazuela over medium heat and sauté the carrots and tomatoes until softened, about five minutes.
Add the ground annatto to the pot and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Stir in the rice, coating each grain with the annatto and oil mixture.
Pour in the chicken broth, add the mustard, salt, and pepper, and bring the mixture to a gentle boil.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the cazuela, and simmer until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed, about fifteen minutes.
While the rice cooks, lay a sheet of parchment over a clean surface and shape small rice clusters into nigiri-like cylinders using wet hands.
Transfer the shaped rice clusters to the cazuela, arranging them in a single layer.
Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella evenly over the rice and return to heat until the cheese melts, about three minutes.
Finish by drizzling lemon juice over the top, tossing with chopped parsley, and serving hot.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
